title: Koszul and quotient reconstruction
statement:
Let $T,A,I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, $P_n=A/I^n$, $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and let $K_\bullet$ be its strict derived quotient tower. In particular $A$ is commutative Noetherian, $A/I$ is additive torsion, and every $P_n$ is finite and perfect over $A$.

Use the sheaf tensor complexes of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] to put
$$Q_m=\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[A_T\xrightarrow{a_j^m}A_T]$$
in cohomological degrees $[-r,0]$, with each transition having degree-minus-one component $a_j$ and degree-zero component $1$. The empty tensor for $r=0$ is $A_T[0]$. Compute derived tensors with a single K-flat representative as in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Write $R\varprojlim$ for the functorial total right derived inverse limit on strict towers of module complexes [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], and define
$$K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}=R\varprojlim_m(K\otimes^L_{A_T}Q_m).$$
Its completion unit $\kappa_K:K\to K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}$ is induced by the compatible degree-zero inclusions $A_T[0]\to Q_m$. Likewise $\operatorname{comp}_K:K\to R\varprojlim K_\bullet$ is induced by the quotient maps. Call $K$ derived $I$-complete if $\kappa_K$ is an isomorphism.

There is a functorial isomorphism
$$c_K:K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim K_\bullet$$
with $c_K\circ\kappa_K=\operatorname{comp}_K$. Consequently every derived $I$-complete $K$ has an isomorphism $\operatorname{comp}_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim K_\bullet$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] with the scheme T, Noetherian ring A and ideal I of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Every P_n is finite, so its last clause identifies the constant sheaf $\underline{A/I^n}$ with $(P_n)_T$ and the limit $B=\varprojlim_n\underline{A/I^n}$ with $A_T$. These identifications are canonical for the finite quotient maps; their projections are the maps $\pi_n$ of the datum. Thus the quotient tower in the item is precisely the completed-coefficient finite-reduction tower, with no identification of the entire constant and completed module categories.

proof.text: Apply the last paragraph of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] on the small pro-etale site of T, with $\widehat A=A_T$, $\mathcal O=\widehat A$ and $N=K$. Step 1 verifies exactly its completed constant coefficient sheaf and finite quotient hypotheses. Its $Q_m(\mathcal O)$ has the same differentials, transition multiplications and degree-zero units as the Koszul tower specified in the statement. Its functorial strict derived inverse limit is the one fixed here. That paragraph gives the canonical comparison between Koszul completion and the finite-reduction derived limit for every $K\in D(A_T)$ and says it respects units. Hence it gives $c_K$ in the actual completed-coefficient category, with $c_K\kappa_K=\operatorname{comp}_K$. The comparisons are induced by the strict quotient augmentations, so maps of K-flat representatives commute with them levelwise and the functorial derived limit gives naturality in K. No equivalence between the entire derived categories is assumed, and no completeness of K is needed for this step.

If K is derived I-complete, its unit $\kappa_K$ is invertible by the definition in the statement. Step 2 gives an invertible $c_K$ and the equality $\operatorname{comp}_K=c_K\kappa_K$. The inverse of $\operatorname{comp}_K$ is $\kappa_K^{-1}c_K^{-1}$: either composite reduces, by associativity and the two inverse identities, to the identity. This proves that the canonical quotient completion map itself is an isomorphism.

blueprint_proof_text:
This is the recorded classical input of the statement, the derived-completion
formalism of Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Section 15.93 (Tag
[091N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/091N)): the Koszul-derived
completion of a complex and the derived limit over its strict quotient tower
compute the same object, and both completion maps are the canonical ones. The
blueprint uses the identification as the defining property of the adic
coefficient datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and gives no
separate proof.

blueprint_update.statement:
For the strict quotient tower $K_\bullet$ of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] there is a functorial isomorphism

$$
 K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim K_\bullet
$$

carrying the Koszul completion map to the quotient-tower completion map
$K\to\Rlim K_\bullet$. Every derived $I$-complete object consequently
satisfies

$$
 K\xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim K_\bullet.
$$
